solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Singular cure for captain

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
to kipper fish is to cure it by salting and smoking

explanation.surface: A doctor's unique remedy for a ship's commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cure' reads as a medical remedy but is the verb for preserving fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the master of a boat or the leader of a sports team, a synonym for captain.

clue.text: Shelter made from loose stones, indefinite number

parts.note: scree is a mass of loose stones on a mountainside
n is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A refuge built out of rubble, quantity unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen is a barrier that protects or hides, a synonym for shelter as a noun.

clue.text: Lay out trendy waistcoat

parts.note: in means fashionable
vest is the American word for a waistcoat

explanation.surface: Spend money on a fashionable waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest money is to lay it out, spend it with an eye to return.

clue.text: Are its pies fresh?

indicators.note: fresh means new, so these letters are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether the bakery's pastries were baked today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' makes PATISSERIE out of ARE ITS PIES; the whole clue is a question one might ask in such a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A pâtisserie is a French pastry shop, where fresh pies would be expected.

clue.text: A rambler right and left

parts.note: over means left over, remaining

explanation.surface: A hiker turning both ways along a footpath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a direction to pair with 'right' but means remaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is one who wanders about, much as a rambler does.

clue.text: Bishop meets girl in country

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Olivia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A churchman has a rendezvous with a young woman somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolivia is a landlocked South American nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: Local worker in bank, sympathetic

parts.note: a bar is a sandbank across a river mouth
tender means gentle and sympathetic

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted employee at a branch of the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British for one's neighbourhood pub; 'bank' suggests money but is a sandbar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves drinks in a pub, so is a worker at the local.

clue.text: Girl, violently ill, supported by youth leader

indicators.note: in a down clue the supported piece sits above the support
violently suggests the letters are thrown about into a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A girl taken badly sick is helped by the head of a youth group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violently' makes LIL; 'supported by' works because in a down entry the sick girl stands on top of her support, the youth leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily is a girl's name, so it can stand for girl in crossword fashion.

clue.text: Lively Spanish port run by old American

parts.note: Vigo is a port in north-west Spain
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
US means American

explanation.surface: A busy Spanish harbour managed by an elderly American.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigorous means full of energy and vitality, a synonym for lively.

clue.text: A pangolin perhaps in area — tent being abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned can mean unrestrained and wild, so the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A scaly creature discovered in a place where a tent has been left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being abandoned' sounds like the tent is deserted, but it rearranges AREA and TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The pangolin is often called the scaly anteater, so it is one example of that animal.

clue.text: Last in bar, I check bolt

indicators.note: the final letter of the word bar is the one wanted here

parts.note: to vet something is to check it over

explanation.surface: Final orders at the pub, and I make sure the door is locked.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivet is a metal pin fastening plates together, a kind of bolt.

clue.text: Flare, easy to carry around?

explanation.surface: A signal flare that is no burden to lug about.
explanation.walkthrough: A VERY LIGHT is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol; read as two words it describes something hardly weighing anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A Very light, named after its inventor Edward Very, is a pistol-fired signal flare; light weight also makes a thing easy to carry.

clue.text: Financial security is what a postie wants?

explanation.surface: A mail carrier dreams of a comfortable income.
explanation.walkthrough: A postie (British for postman) would love a road that is easy to walk, hence an easy street.
explanation.definitionFit: Living on easy street is an idiom for comfortable wealth; a simple round would suit a mail carrier.

clue.text: A recurrent air?

indicators.note: recurrent is read as running back, so the word air is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: A tune that keeps coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera, an air that may well be repeated.

clue.text: Rest after musical game for children

indicators.note: after puts the resting place behind the show

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical
to cradle something is to rest or support it gently

explanation.surface: Children play a game after taking a break from a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's cradle is a string game played by children, looping string between the fingers.

clue.text: It's one's characteristic habit to back the Constitution?

parts.note: to second a motion is to back or support it
one's constitution is one's basic make-up or nature

explanation.surface: Supporting the nation's founding law comes naturally to some people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitution' looks political with its capital, but it means physical and mental make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Second nature is an idiom for behaviour so ingrained it seems innate.

clue.text: Arranged grandiose changes

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of the following word are altered in order

explanation.surface: Ostentatious alterations were planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Organised means arranged or put in order, a synonym.

clue.text: Ordinary copper makes a register of eye experts

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to list is to register or record

explanation.surface: An ordinary policeman compiles a roll of optometrists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer but is the metal; 'register' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Oculists are specialists in eyes and their treatment, as the Latin oculus suggests.

clue.text: Miss boxing star in US city

indicators.note: boxing means putting in a box, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a lass is a young woman or miss
Vega is a bright star in the constellation Lyra

explanation.surface: A young woman puts a famous boxer into an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing star' reads as a prizefighter but splits into a container indicator and a celestial body.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Vegas is a city in Nevada famous for gambling, an example of a US city.

clue.text: Commuter initially running fast to get to other side of station

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word Commuter is used

parts.note: haring is running quickly, like a hare
to cross is to go over to the far side

explanation.surface: A commuter sprints for a train at a busy London terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARING CROSS is a major railway terminus in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Charing Cross is a London railway station, an example of a station.

clue.text: Notice article about details in programme

indicators.note: about signals one set of letters going round another

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
gen is British slang for information or details
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A poster gives particulars within a schedule of events.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to deal with, a programme for a meeting.

clue.text: Last cut — heart, again!

indicators.note: cut signals the word is docked of its final letter

parts.note: the end is the last part
the core is the heart or centre

explanation.surface: A final reduction, then a cry of passion repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Encore is the cry of an audience wanting a performance repeated, meaning again!

clue.text: Nothing left? Almost gone

indicators.note: almost signals a word missing its final letter

parts.note: over means finished or gone

explanation.surface: Is there nothing remaining? It has nearly all disappeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is zero in tennis scoring, so it means nothing.

clue.text: Flower in picture, next to paper kite

parts.note: a snap is a snapshot photograph
a dragon is an old name for a paper kite, often dragon-shaped

explanation.surface: A bloom pictured beside a child's kite.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, or antirrhinum, is a garden plant with showy blooms, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Finished a lasagne?

parts.note: past means over or finished

explanation.surface: Has someone polished off a plate of baked noodles?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows lasagne is only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is one type of Italian pasta, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Some mousetraps evident in part of church

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Signs of mice traps are visible in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: They may help one along the way

definitions.text: They may help one along the way

parts.words: They may help one along the way
parts.note: reads like supportive friends but literally describes direction markers on a road

explanation.surface: Kind people who assist someone on life's journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Signposts are roadside markers showing travellers which route to take.

clue.text: Wild dog shot after row

indicators.note: after places the attempt following the noise

parts.note: a din is a loud row or racket
a go is a shot or attempt

explanation.surface: An untamed animal is gunned down following a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire but means an attempt; 'row' is a noisy row, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is the feral dog of Australia, an example of a wild canine.

clue.text: Delay South American writer and daughter

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
US means American
a pen is a writing instrument
D is the genealogy abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A Latin American author and his child hold things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one phrase but splits into S and US.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to postpone or put off, a synonym for delay.

clue.text: Mean to declare silver (English)

parts.note: to aver is to state or declare firmly
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone intends to announce an English silver item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as a verb ('intend') but is the arithmetical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The average of a set of numbers is its arithmetic mean.
